terminal_record.title: The Atlantic’s “Unthinkable” Project Ranked 50 Trump-Era Incidents
terminal_record.description_short: The Atlantic catalogued 50 incidents from Trump’s first term, ranking them subjectively by outlandishness and importance.
terminal_record.description_medium: The Atlantic described its “Unthinkable” project as a catalog of 50 incidents from the midpoint of Trump’s first term, ranked subjectively for outlandishness and importance. A linked explainer was published January 14, 2019. The available material supports the magazine’s editorial project and framing, not a measured democratic-stability effect or a continuing risk signal in March 2026.
terminal_record.description_long: The Atlantic’s landing page introduces “Donald Trump’s 50 Most Unthinkable Moments” as a review of 50 incidents from the first Trump presidency. The magazine says it chose incidents it considered improbable, norm-bending, and destructive, and explicitly describes its ranking as highly subjective, based on outlandishness and importance. A linked video explainer featuring editor in chief Jeffrey Goldberg was published January 14, 2019, and explains the project as an attempt to chronicle bizarre and dangerous moments of the presidency. These sources document an editorial catalog and the publication’s own description of its selection. They do not show that the magazine measured democratic stability, identified a mitigation plan, or continued to issue a specific risk signal in March 2026. The frozen record’s March 4, 2026 date and continuing-risk wording are not retained because the accessible evidence connects the project to the 2019 midterm of Trump’s first term. January 14 is the linked explainer’s publication date and earliest archive capture date for the landing page; the landing page’s original release timestamp remains uncertain. This entry describes editorial coverage, not an independent finding of harm.
terminal_record.date_precision: The Atlantic explainer and earliest accessible archived landing page are dated January 14, 2019; the original landing-page release timestamp is not exposed.

So we decided to pause for a moment and analyze 50 of the most improbable, norm-bending, and destructive incidents of this presidency to date.

terminal_record.title: Trump's February 25 Memorandum Targets Covington & Burling
terminal_record.description_short: Trump's February 25, 2025 memorandum directed clearance suspensions for specified Covington lawyers and federal reviews of the firm's engagements and contracts.
terminal_record.description_medium: On February 25, 2025, Donald Trump signed a presidential memorandum directing agencies to suspend specified Covington & Burling security clearances pending review, terminate federal engagements where permitted by law, and have OMB review the firm's contracts. The source identifies a memorandum, not a March 14 executive order. The documents establish directives, not their eventual implementation or outcome.
terminal_record.description_long: On February 25, 2025, Donald Trump signed a presidential memorandum titled “Suspension of Security Clearances and Evaluation of Government Contracts.” It directed executive departments and agencies to take lawful steps to suspend active clearances held by Peter Koski and Covington & Burling members, partners, and employees who assisted former Special Counsel Jack Smith, pending a review of their roles and responsibilities. The memo also directed agencies to take steps to terminate Covington engagements to the maximum extent permitted by law and consistent with a separate Office of Management and Budget memorandum. It instructed OMB to issue a memorandum directing all agencies to review government contracts with the firm. The White House described the action as a memorandum and stated its rationale in terms of “weaponization of the judicial process”; that is the administration’s stated justification, not an independently established finding about the lawyers. The official documents verify issuance and the directions. They do not show whether clearances were ultimately suspended, contracts ended, or engagements terminated. The stored March 14, 2025 date and “executive order” label are incorrect for this action. This record covers the February 25 memorandum and its stated directives only.

source_fact_map.fact: The action was a February 25, 2025 presidential memorandum.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
February 25, 2025

MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF STATE THE SECRETARY OF DEFENSE THE ATTORNEY GENERAL THE SECRETARY OF ENERGY THE DIRECTOR OF THE OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET THE DIRECTOR OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE THE DIRECTOR OF THE CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY THE DIRECTOR OF THE OFFICE OF PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT

SUBJECT: Suspension of Security Clearances and Evaluation of Government Contracts I hereby direct the Attorney General and all other relevant heads of executive departments and agencies (agencies) to immediately take steps consistent with applicable law to suspend any active security clearances held by Peter Koski and all members, partners, and employees of Covington & Burling LLP who assisted former Special Counsel Jack Smith during his time as Special Counsel, pending a review and determination of their roles and responsibilities, if any, in the weaponization of the judicial process. I also direct the Attorney General and heads of agencies to take such actions as are necessary to terminate any engagement of Covington & Burling LLP by any agency to the maximum extent permitted by law and consistent with the memorandum that shall be issued by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. Additionally, if any of the covered Covington & Burling LLP members, partners, and employees referenced in this memorandum obtained a security clearance from an agency not included as an addressee of this memorandum, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall provide this memorandum to the appropriate clearance-granting agency to ensure compliance. I further direct the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to issue a memorandum to all agencies to review all Government contracts with Covington & Burling LLP.

source_fact_map.fact: The memorandum directed lawful steps to suspend clearances held by named Covington personnel who assisted Jack Smith, pending review.
